candidates.label: trans: partner bank and partner account missing together
candidates.note: Structural: cash operations have no counterparty. Expected to equal the number of non-transfer operations.
candidates.sql: SELECT count(*) FROM stg.trans WHERE partner_bank IS NULL AND partner_account IS NULL

candidates.label: trans: three different encodings of 'no value' in the same column
candidates.note: raw.trans.k_symbol arrives as quoted empty string, unquoted empty field (NULL) and a single space. Three spellings of the same fact.
candidates.sql: SELECT count(*) FROM raw.trans WHERE k_symbol IS NULL OR k_symbol = '' OR btrim(k_symbol) = ''

candidates.label: trans: structural NULL in operation (interest postings have no operation)
candidates.note: Every one of these is an interest credit (k_symbol = UROK). The NULL is meaningful, not missing, so it must not be imputed.
candidates.sql: SELECT count(*) FROM stg.trans WHERE operation_code IS NULL

candidates.label: trans: negative balance after the transaction
candidates.note: Overdrafts. Real banking behaviour, not a defect; relevant to Q9 because they drag the average balance down and must not be clipped.
candidates.sql: SELECT count(*) FROM stg.trans WHERE balance_after < 0

candidates.label: client district differs from the district of the account they own
candidates.note: Not a defect: a client may bank in a different district than they live in. It is a modelling fork for Q1 and Q5, which is why both questions state which district they use.
candidates.sql: SELECT count(*) FROM stg.disp d JOIN stg.client c USING (client_id) JOIN stg.account a ON a.account_id = d.account_id WHERE d.disp_type_code = 'OWNER' AND c.district_id <> a.district_id

candidates.label: trans: intra-day ordering is undefined (accounts with >1 posting on their last date)
candidates.note: The closing balance of a day is only well defined if the last posting of that day is identifiable. trans_id is not chronological within a day, so for these accounts the closing balance is a choice, not a fact.
candidates.sql: SELECT count(*) FROM ( SELECT account_id, trans_date, count(*) AS n, row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY account_id ORDER BY trans_date DESC) AS rn FROM stg.trans GROUP BY account_id, trans_date ) x WHERE rn = 1 AND n > 1

candidates.label: trans: running balance does not reconcile per account (tolerance 1.00 CZK)
candidates.note: Order independent test: the sum of signed amounts should equal the last reported balance. Differences cluster at 0.1-0.5 CZK (rounding), but a tail of accounts is off by hundreds, which is a real gap.
candidates.sql: WITH final AS ( SELECT account_id, balance_after FROM ( SELECT account_id, balance_after, row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY account_id ORDER BY trans_date DESC, trans_id DESC) AS rn FROM stg.trans ) x WHERE rn = 1 ), summed AS ( SELECT account_id, sum(signed_amount) AS total FROM stg.trans GROUP BY 1 ) SELECT count(*) FROM summed s JOIN final f USING (account_id) WHERE abs(s.total - f.balance_after) > 1.00

candidates.label: owner was younger than 15 at account opening
candidates.note: Implausible for a legal account holder. Minimum observed age is 10.3 years. Affects Q7 (average age at loan start) and Q8.
candidates.sql: SELECT count(*) FROM stg.disp d JOIN stg.client c USING (client_id) JOIN stg.account a ON a.account_id = d.account_id WHERE d.disp_type_code = 'OWNER' AND (a.open_date - c.birth_date) / 365.25 < 15

candidates.label: trans: running balance off by more than 100 CZK per account
candidates.note: Material, not rounding: a missing or extra posting. Directly affects Q9.
candidates.sql: WITH final AS ( SELECT account_id, balance_after FROM ( SELECT account_id, balance_after, row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY account_id ORDER BY trans_date DESC, trans_id DESC) AS rn FROM stg.trans ) x WHERE rn = 1 ), summed AS ( SELECT account_id, sum(signed_amount) AS total FROM stg.trans GROUP BY 1 ) SELECT count(*) FROM summed s JOIN final f USING (account_id) WHERE abs(s.total - f.balance_after) > 100.00

candidates.label: trans: amount is zero
candidates.note: Zero-value postings (sanction interest and interest with no accrual). Breaks a naive 'amount > 0' validity rule but changes no sum.
candidates.sql: SELECT count(*) FROM stg.trans WHERE amount = 0

candidates.label: owner was younger than 15 at loan start
candidates.note: A minor cannot take a loan. Direct hit on Q7.
candidates.sql: SELECT count(*) FROM stg.loan l JOIN stg.disp d ON d.account_id = l.account_id AND d.disp_type_code = 'OWNER' JOIN stg.client c USING (client_id) WHERE (l.loan_date - c.birth_date) / 365.25 < 15

candidates.label: district: placeholder '?' in 1995 unemployment and crime columns
candidates.note: Known original-dataset gap (district 69, Jesenik). Only matters once a metric uses the 1995 columns; none of the 10 questions does.
candidates.sql: SELECT count(*) FROM stg.district WHERE unemployment_rate_1995_raw IS NOT NULL OR crimes_1995_raw IS NOT NULL

candidates.label: trans: duplicate business key (same account, date, type, amount, balance)
candidates.note: Distinct trans_id, identical business content. A duplicate posting the primary key cannot catch.
candidates.sql: SELECT coalesce(sum(n) - count(*), 0) FROM ( SELECT count(*) AS n FROM stg.trans GROUP BY account_id, trans_date, trans_type_code, coalesce(operation_code, '~'), amount, balance_after HAVING count(*) > 1 ) d

candidates.label: card: holder is a disponent rather than the account owner
candidates.note: Q4 and Q8 ask about the card of the account OWNER, so a card held by a disponent must not be attributed to the owner.
candidates.sql: SELECT count(*) FROM stg.card k JOIN stg.disp d USING (disp_id) WHERE d.disp_type_code <> 'OWNER'

candidates.label: account has no transaction at all
candidates.note: Would make the account invisible in any transaction-derived metric, including the Q9 balance.
candidates.sql: SELECT count(*) FROM stg.account a WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM stg.trans t WHERE t.account_id = a.account_id)

candidates.label: business date outside the configured plausibility window
candidates.note: Window is 1993-01-01 to 1998-12-31 (src.config). A date outside it silently corrupts every per-year and per-month grouping (Q2, Q5, Q6).
candidates.sql: SELECT (SELECT count(*) FROM stg.account WHERE open_date NOT BETWEEN %(lo)s AND %(hi)s) + (SELECT count(*) FROM stg.loan WHERE loan_date NOT BETWEEN %(lo)s AND %(hi)s) + (SELECT count(*) FROM stg.card WHERE issued_date NOT BETWEEN %(lo)s AND %(hi)s) + (SELECT count(*) FROM stg.trans WHERE trans_date NOT BETWEEN %(lo)s AND %(hi)s)

candidates.label: unparsable date or amount anywhere in staging
candidates.note: Non-zero means a cast silently produced NULL. The raw text is kept in the *_raw audit columns, so nothing is lost and the rows are countable.
candidates.sql: SELECT (SELECT count(*) FROM stg.account WHERE open_date_raw IS NOT NULL) + (SELECT count(*) FROM stg.loan WHERE loan_date_raw IS NOT NULL) + (SELECT count(*) FROM stg.card WHERE issued_raw IS NOT NULL) + (SELECT count(*) FROM stg.trans WHERE trans_date_raw IS NOT NULL) + (SELECT count(*) FROM stg.loan WHERE amount_raw IS NOT NULL) + (SELECT count(*) FROM stg.trans WHERE amount_raw IS NOT NULL) + (SELECT count(*) FROM stg.trans WHERE balance_raw IS NOT NULL)
